Find the bugs your users would hit, before they hit them.

Most bugs that reach users are not in code nobody tested. They are in paths nobody walked: rejecting instead of approving, the empty account, the second tab, someone else's id in the URL. Crashtest is a macOS app with an autonomous agent that walks those paths for you.

## Built with the neatHack tools

| Tool | How Crashtest uses it |
|---|---|
| [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com) | Every phase is its own traced workflow (`repo-inventory`, `scenario-generation`, `app-bootstrap`, `scenario-sweep`, `app-recovery`, `project-chat`), grouped per project. Two custom detections — **Bug found by Crashtest** and **Unverified verdict** — and before/after traces drove real fixes. Our own build sessions are traced too. [Evidence](docs/evidence/neatlogs-baselines.md) |
| [Entire](https://entire.io) | Checkpoints on our commits, plus **Entire Graph inside the product**: the inventory and sweep agents get graph search / definitions / callers / blast-radius tools over the repo under test. |
| [cfo.ai](https://cfo.ai) | Business plan for Crashtest: pricing, unit costs taken from neatlogs traces, revenue scenarios and runway. |

## Run it

Requirements: macOS, Node 22+, git. Optional: the [Entire CLI](https://entire.io) for graph tools.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open **Settings**, add your Anthropic API key (and a GitHub token for private repos, or SSH details for a VDS), then paste a GitHub link into the chat.

content.text:
Entire tarafı bitti: repo entire.io'da açık ve iki checkpoint orada, hiçbir şifre ya da anahtar sızmadı.

**Türkçe meselesi:** Commit'ler, README ve kod tamamen İngilizce. Ekranda gördüğün "devam et" senin bana yazdığın ilk mesaj; Entire oturumu o mesajla başlıklandırıyor, ben değiştiremem. Public tarafta görünmesini istemiyorsan bana İngilizce yazman yeterli. Benim cevaplarım da transcript'te görünüyor, o yüzden ikimiz de İngilizce yazarsak sayfa tamamen İngilizce görünür. Sen nasıl istersen.

**Kaçırmadan yakaladığım bir sorun:** Son commit'in checkpoint'i yanlışlıkla eski oturuma bağlanmıştı. O oturumun kayıtlarında AWS hesap ID'si ve IAM kullanıcı adı vardı (şifre gizlenmişti). Push etmeden fark ettim:
- O checkpoint'i sildim ve eski oturumun Entire'daki kalıntısını temizledim.
- Hesap ID'si ve kullanıcı adı için de gizleme kuralı ekledim.
- Checkpoint'i yeniden oluşturdum ve taradım. İçinde ne anahtar ne şifre var; kalanlar sunucu ID'si gibi zararsız şeyler.

**Şu an entire.io'da görünenler:**
- Repo: https://entire.io/gh/emreozyoruk/crashtest
- Checkpoint'ler: `97c75579b386` ve `c274ac2e0387`. Linkleri README'de ve build log'da var.

**Senden başka bir şey gerekmiyor.** Sıradaki işlerim:
- cfo.ai planını bitirmek: kötümser senaryoda paranın hangi ay bittiği, bir özet grafik, kısa açıklama ve README'ye link.
- Sonra bütün P1 senaryolarıyla büyük demo koşusu.

entries.description:
Input constraint: Provide parameters for exactly one of: (list) or (read).

Finds Canvas components and templates without attaching them to chat. list returns compact catalog matches; read returns selected instructions, each component's props skeleton, and runtime requirements. Requires the workspace's Canvas template feature. Entries are building guidance, not saved blocks or rendered-output evidence; reads never create model data.

_context.description: Optional active scenario, page, and time zone.

kind.description: Without it, list includes both components and templates.

query.description: Search words; an entry matches when any word appears in its title, description, tags, aliases, or decision outcomes. Without it, list returns every entry that matches kind.

org_id.description: Workspace ID or slug. Optional when you belong to one workspace. Otherwise, call list_orgs and choose an ID or slug. Numbers always identify workspace IDs.

target.description: Catalog targets returned by list, or exact entry names; one read resolves templates and components together. Unknown or ambiguous names return unresolved entries instead of guessing.

input_schema.description: Fill exactly one action block: list, read.

add_text.markdown:
## Crashtest business plan

**What we sell.** Crashtest maps every user scenario in a repo and runs them for real in a browser. Two plans:

- **Pro, $29 / month**: bring your own Anthropic key. The customer pays model costs directly, so Pro has almost no cost of revenue.
- **Cloud, $299 / month**: we run the agents and the sandbox. About 600 scenario runs and 4 repo inventories per customer per month.

**Unit costs come from real neatlogs traces of the agent**, not guesses:

- Scenario run: **$0.117**, the mean of 8 `scenario-sweep` traces on Conduit ($0.070 to $0.159).
- Repo inventory: **$0.815**, the `repo-inventory` trace after the tool-scoping fix. It was $0.461 before; the fix doubled the cost but found 24% more surfaces.
- Sandbox: **$20 per Cloud customer per month**. This is an *assumption* based on a t3.small-class VM.

That gives a Cloud customer about $93 of cost on $299 of revenue, and a blended gross margin of about **79%**.

**Scenarios** (only growth, churn and hiring change between them):

| | New customer growth / month (Pro, Cloud) | Monthly churn (Pro, Cloud) | Engineer hire |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | 10%, 8% | 5%, 3% | month 6 |
| Upside | 15%, 12% | 4%, 2% | month 6 |
| Downside | 5%, 4% | 7%, 5% | month 18 |

**What the model says**

- **Base:** cash bottoms at about **$7.7k in March 2028**, and monthly cash flow turns positive in **April 2028**.
- **Upside:** about **$521k** of cash by December 2028.
- **Downside:** if we still hire at month 6, cash runs out in **November 2027**. Moving the hire to month 18 keeps the low point at about **$51k**. **The engineer hire is the decision that sets our runway.** Hire only when MRR crosses about $15k.

**Assumptions to replace with real data:** opening cash of $150k (pre-seed, *assumed*), founder pay of $8k, engineer pay of $12k, marketing at 10% of revenue, and first-month signups of 10 Pro and 2 Cloud. Every input is editable on this page, and every output recomputes from them.

update_text.markdown:
**What we sell.** Crashtest maps every user scenario in a repo and runs them for real in a browser. Two plans:

- **Pro, $29 / month**: bring your own Anthropic key. The customer pays model costs directly, so Pro has almost no cost of revenue.
- **Cloud, $299 / month**: we run the agents and the sandbox. About 600 scenario runs and 4 repo inventories per customer per month.

**Unit costs come from real neatlogs traces of the agent**, not guesses:

- Scenario run: **$0.117**, the mean of 8 `scenario-sweep` traces on Conduit ($0.070 to $0.159).
- Repo inventory: **$0.815**, the `repo-inventory` trace after the tool-scoping fix. It was $0.461 before; the fix doubled the cost but found 24% more surfaces.
- Sandbox: **$20 per Cloud customer per month**. This is an *assumption* based on a t3.small-class VM.

That gives a Cloud customer about $93 of cost on $299 of revenue, and a blended gross margin of about **79%**.

**Scenarios.** Only growth, churn and hiring change between them:

- **Base:** new-customer growth of 10% a month for Pro and 8% for Cloud; churn of 5% and 3%; engineer hired at month 6.
- **Upside:** growth of 15% and 12%; churn of 4% and 2%; engineer at month 6.
- **Downside:** growth of 5% and 4%; churn of 7% and 5%; engineer at month 18.

**What the model says**

- **Base:** cash bottoms at about **$7.7k in March 2028**, and monthly cash flow turns positive in **April 2028**.
- **Upside:** about **$521k** of cash by December 2028.
- **Downside:** if we still hire at month 6, cash runs out in **November 2027**. Moving the hire to month 18 keeps the low point at about **$51k**. **The engineer hire is the decision that sets our runway.** Hire only when MRR crosses about $15k.

**Assumptions to replace with real data:** opening cash of $150k (pre-seed, *assumed*), founder pay of $8k, engineer pay of $12k, marketing at 10% of revenue, and first-month signups of 10 Pro and 2 Cloud. Every input is editable on this page, and every output recomputes from them. Switch the scenario in the sidebar to see Upside and Downside.

# cfo.ai evidence

The Crashtest business plan is a live model in cfo.ai, built through the cfo.ai MCP server
from this repo's Claude Code session.

- Base scenario: https://app.cfo.ai/s/--rWFPOxuMvaL0nN
- Upside: https://app.cfo.ai/s/C9DgOonrAXn3DhqQ
- Downside: https://app.cfo.ai/s/e_GPD5Z-hJGywRX7

## How the model is built

| Table | What it holds |
|---|---|
| Plan assumptions | Per plan (Pro, Cloud): price, first-month signups, monthly new-customer growth, monthly churn |
| Unit costs and operating inputs | Cost per scenario run, cost per repo inventory, runs and repos per Cloud customer, sandbox cost, pay, hire month, tools, marketing share, opening cash |
| Customers and revenue | Monthly, by plan: new customers → paying customers (churned) → revenue |
| P&L and cash | Revenue, cost of revenue, gross profit and margin, payroll, marketing, tools, operating expenses, net cash flow, cash balance, runway in months |

| Sandbox per Cloud customer | $20 / month | Assumption: t3.small-class VM, the size our VDS test used |

## Results (Oct 2026 – Dec 2028)

| Scenario | Lowest cash | Cash in Dec 2028 | Note |
|---|---|---|---|

| Downside, hire at month 18 | $51k (Dec 2028) | $51k | The fix the plan recommends |

assumptions, labelled as such in the model.
EOF

user: Product: Conduit (RealWorld example app)
What it does: Conduit is a Medium-style blogging platform. Users register, write markdown articles with tags, comment, favorite articles and follow other authors. It has a React/Vite single-page frontend and an Express/Sequelize REST backend under /api.
App type: web+api
Stack: Node.js, Express 5, Sequelize 6 (config dialect from env, mysql in .env.example; pg installed), JWT (jsonwebtoken), bcrypt, React 19, Vite 7, react-router-dom 7 (HashRouter), axios, markdown-to-jsx, react-paginate
All journeys, in order: Browse the home page and discover articles → Sign up and sign in → Read an article and its comments → Write, edit and delete an article → Comment on an article → Favorite articles and follow authors → View profiles → Edit settings and log out

user: Product: Conduit (RealWorld example app)
What it does: Conduit is a Medium-style blogging platform. Users register, write markdown articles with tags, comment, favorite articles and follow other authors. It has a React/Vite single-page frontend and an Express/Sequelize REST backend under /api.
App type: web+api
Stack: Node.js, Express 5, Sequelize 6 (config dialect from env, mysql in .env.example; pg installed), JWT (jsonwebtoken), bcrypt, React 19, Vite 7, react-router-dom 7 (HashRouter), axios, markdown-to-jsx, react-paginate
All journeys, in order: Browse the home page and discover articles → Sign up and sign in → Read an article and its comments → Write, edit and delete an article → Comment on an article → Favorite articles and follow authors → View profiles → Edit settings and log out

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.description: Create a detection in this project and start a 14-day backfill so it immediately scores recent traces. For regex / conditional types, run preview_detection FIRST and only create if it flags > 0 spans; classifier / pii are created directly. Needs a group_id from list_detection_groups (or create_detection_group).

display_name.description: Human-readable name shown in the dashboard.

group_id.description: UUID of the group this detection belongs to. Get one from list_detection_groups (or create_detection_group). Required.

type.description: Detection type. classifier: preset ML model (jailbreaking|nsfw|hate|refusals). regex: pattern match on input/output. conditional: field/operator rule tree. pii: entity detection.

config.description: Type-specific config. classifier: {classifier_slug:'jailbreaking'|'nsfw'|'hate'|'refusals'}. regex: {input_pattern?, output_pattern?, operator?='OR', case_sensitive?=false} (at least one pattern). conditional: {root:{type:'group', logic:'AND'|'OR', children:[...]}}. pii: {entities?:['EMAIL_ADDRESS','PHONE_NUMBER',...]} (omit = all).

description.description: Short description of what the detection flags.

run_on.description: Where the detection runs. Omit for per-trace. span_types required for frequency='span_type'; span_names required for frequency='span_name'.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__get_detection_trend
entries.description: Get hourly / daily / weekly occurrence counts for a single detection (e.g. Hallucination, Jailbreak Attempt, Task Failure). Use this to spot regressions and spikes after a deploy. Pair with `list_detections` to discover which detection names are enabled on the project.

detection_name.description: Detection name. Matched flexibly against the project's detection list — both the friendly snake_case form (`jailbreak_attempt`, `hallucination`, `nsfw_content`) and the UI display name (`Jailbreak Attempt Detector`, `NSFW Content`) work, case-insensitive, with common suffixes like `Detector` / `Monitor` ignored. Call `list_detections` first if you want the canonical list of names enabled on this project.

period.description: Lookback window for the trend. Default `7d`.

granularity.description: Bucket size. Defaults to `hour` for `24h` and `day` for `7d`/`30d`.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__list_detections
entries.description: List all active detections enabled on this project. A detection is a rule (regex / classifier / conditional) that flags spans matching a pattern — e.g. Hallucination, Jailbreak Attempt, Task Failure, User Frustration. Use this to discover which `detection_name` values are valid for `get_detection_trend`, or to answer 'what is this project monitoring for?'

group_id.description: Optional group UUID to scope the listing (e.g. only Safety detections). Omit to list every active detection.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__preview_detection
entries.description: Dry-run a regex or conditional detection against recent traces without saving it. Returns total_count (how many spans it would flag) plus sample matches. ALWAYS call this before create_detection for regex / conditional types, and only create if total_count > 0.

type.description: Detection type to preview. Only regex and conditional are previewable; classifier and pii cannot be previewed — create those directly.

config.description: Type-specific config. regex: {input_pattern?, output_pattern?, operator?='OR', case_sensitive?=false} (at least one pattern). conditional: {root: {type:'group', logic:'AND'|'OR', children:[{type:'rule', field, operator, value}]}}.

run_on.description: Where the detection runs. Omit for per-trace.

timeframe_days.description: How many days back to scan (default backend-side).

# Crashtest

**Find the bugs your users would hit, before they hit them.**

Most bugs that reach users are not in code nobody tested. They are in paths nobody walked: rejecting instead of approving, the empty account, the second tab, someone else's id in the URL. Crashtest is a macOS app with an autonomous agent that walks those paths for you.

Give it a GitHub repo and it:

1. **Maps the app from its code** — screens, actions, API operations, background jobs, integrations, roles, entity lifecycles, limits.
2. **Writes every scenario a user can do or live through**, ranked P1–P3 and grouped by user journey.
3. **Runs them for real** — clones the app, boots it on your Mac or on your own server (VDS), drives it in a browser, and reports what broke with a screenshot, the root cause at `file:line`, and a suggested diff. It never edits your code.

Built during [neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) (Oct 10–12, 2026). Build log: [hackathon.md](hackathon.md).

## What it found on its first real target

On [TonyMckes/conduit-realworld-example-app](https://github.com/TonyMckes/conduit-realworld-example-app), a well-known RealWorld implementation, Crashtest wrote 245 scenarios, booted the app from scratch (local Postgres, generated `.env`, API + frontend) and found, among others:

- **A comment can be deleted through any article's URL** — `backend/controllers/comments.js` ignores the slug.
- **Users can follow themselves** — `backend/controllers/profiles.js` never compares ids.
- `DEV_DB_LOGGING="false"` crashes the app at boot, because the string `"false"` is truthy.

Details, diffs and screenshots: [docs/evidence/findings-conduit.md](docs/evidence/findings-conduit.md).

## How it works

```
GitHub link ─► Intake ─► Inventory agent ─► Scenario writer ─► [Start] ─► Local │ VDS
               clone,     Sonnet 5.5,        Haiku 5.5,                     │
               products   read-only tools    parallel per journey           ▼
                                                              Bootstrap agent ─► Sweep agent
                                                              boots the app      one scenario at a time,
                                                              (shell, logs,      Playwright browser + API,
                                                              ports, recovery)   verdict + root cause + diff
```

- **Agents** run on the [Claude Agent SDK](https://docs.claude.com/en/api/agent-sdk/overview) with a per-phase tool set: the inventory agent can only read; the bootstrap and sweep agents operate the app through Crashtest's own MCP tools (`shell`, `start_background`, `read_log`, `expose_port`, `http_get`).
- **Local and VDS are the same to the agent.** Both runtimes implement those tools; the VDS runtime works over SSH and tunnels the app's ports back so the browser on your Mac can drive it.
- **Recovery.** If the app stops answering mid-run, Crashtest restarts it with the commands the bootstrap agent used and carries on. Services run in the foreground and are always stopped at the end, even if you quit mid-run.
- **Chat.** Ask about the app, hand over `.env` values or server details (stored encrypted in the macOS Keychain), or start a run from the conversation.
npm run dev
```

Open **Settings**, add your Anthropic API key (and a GitHub token for private repos, or SSH details for a VDS), then paste a GitHub link into the chat.

## License

MIT
```

open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

## Post 2 — first real bugs (post now)
Day 1 of #neatHack: Crashtest is alive.

Gave it a public repo (RealWorld "Conduit"). It read the code, wrote 294 user scenarios, booted the app itself (Postgres, .env, API, frontend) and found real bugs:

Our agent kept reaching for a tool it wasn't allowed to use. Telling it "there is no shell" in the prompt didn't help.

**What broke:** Malformed JWT on follow/unfollow returns 500 instead of 401

**What broke:** JWT never expires and is not invalidated after a password change
### S-052 [P1] Old token still works after logout
**What broke:** Logout does not invalidate the JWT server-side; token is still valid after logout and never expires
### S-154 [P1] Post a comment with an expired or forged token
**What broke:** Expired or forged JWT returns 500 instead of 401

**What broke:** Settings update accepts a username that is already taken

**What broke:** Article list endpoint returns 500 with raw DB errors for negative or non-numeric limit/offset, and doesn't cap limit

**What broke:** Updating an article title to one already used by another article is accepted (200) and creates a duplicate slug
### S-274 [P1] Handle a negative or non-numeric limit and offset
**What broke:** Negative or non-numeric limit/offset on GET /api/articles causes 500; no cap on limit

**What broke:** Duplicate-email signup returns errors.body 'Email already exists.. try logging in' instead of errors.email 'has already been taken'

**What broke:** POST /api/users/login has no rate limiting, lockout, or CAPTCHA — brute-forceable
### S-272 [P1] Register with a duplicate username and get a validation error
**What broke:** POST /api/users accepts a duplicate username (201) instead of 422
### S-111 [P1] Publish a new article with tags from the editor
**What broke:** Editor tags input has no Enter-to-add behaviour; pressing Enter submits the form with only the first tag
### S-118 [P1] Double-click Publish creates only one article
**What broke:** Double-click Publish creates duplicate articles (same slug); no in-flight guard
### S-151 [P1] Reject posting a comment with an empty body
**What broke:** Empty comment is silently ignored client-side; no request, no 422, no 'can't be blank' error shown
### S-155 [P1] Double-click Post Comment
**What broke:** Post Comment button is not disabled while the comment request is in flight
### S-037 [P1] Two simultaneous sign-ups with the same email from two tabs
**What broke:** Duplicate accounts can be created with the same email (concurrent sign-up race)
### S-112 [P1] Reject publish when the title is empty
**What broke:** 422 validation error for missing article title is keyed under errors.body instead of errors.title
### S-117 [P1] Lose the network during publish
**What broke:** Publishing while offline navigates to #/article/undefined instead of showing a network error
### S-127 [P1] Article in a stale editor after author logs out and another signs in
**What broke:** Stale editor tab keeps sending the logged-out author's token, so the article is changed after logout and a different user's login
### S-193 [P1] Following yourself is refused
**What broke:** A user can follow themselves via POST /api/profiles/:username/follow

| File | Broken scenarios | What is wrong |
|---|---|---|

"""

Observed: I signed in as a fresh user and changed only the bio. I left the password blank and clicked Update Settings. I did not inspect the settings-save response or the bio value after the save. A screenshot of the page after the update is saved.
Finding: Summary: Saving settings with a blank password overwrites the stored password, so the original password stops working
Expected: A blank password leaves the existing password untouched, and logging in with the original password still works.
Actual: The update re-hashes the blank or undefined password and saves it. Login with the original password then fails with 'Wrong email/password combination'.
RootCause: backend/controllers/user.js:36 uses `password !== undefined || password !== ""`. This is always true, so line 37 always runs bcryptHash on the blank or undefined password and replaces the stored hash.
SuggestedFix: --- a/backend/controllers/user.js
+++ b/backend/controllers/user.js
@@ -36,1 +36,1 @@
-    if (password !== undefined || password !== "") {
+    if (password !== undefined && password !== "") {

Finding: Summary: A user can follow themselves via POST /api/profiles/:username/follow
Expected: A 4xx rejection, and no self-follow row. The follower count stays at 0.
Actual: 200 OK. The profile shows following:true and followersCount:1 for the user's own profile.
RootCause: backend/controllers/profiles.js:39-40. followToggler calls profile.addFollower(loggedUser) without checking that loggedUser is not the target profile.

# Crashtest (neatHack, 10–12 Ekim 2026)

Bir GitHub reposunu verince uygulamanın kodunu okuyan, kullanıcının yaşayabileceği tüm senaryoları yazan ve bunları gerçek tarayıcıda deneyip bug bulan Mac uygulaması. neatHack için yapıldı.

## Linkler
- Repo: https://github.com/emreozyoruk/crashtest
- Entire (checkpoint'ler): https://entire.io/gh/emreozyoruk/crashtest
- cfo.ai iş planı: https://app.cfo.ai/s/--rWFPOxuMvaL0nN (Upside: https://app.cfo.ai/s/C9DgOonrAXn3DhqQ · Downside: https://app.cfo.ai/s/e_GPD5Z-hJGywRX7)
- Build log: repodaki hackathon.md

## Kararlar
- Fiyat: Pro $29/ay (kullanıcı kendi Anthropic anahtarını getirir), Cloud $299/ay (biz çalıştırırız).
- Maliyetler neatlogs'tan: senaryo başına ~$0.12, repo haritası ~$0.8.
- cfo.ai'ın söylediği: ilk mühendisi işe alma zamanı runway'i belirliyor; tarihe göre değil gelire göre (MRR ~$15k) işe alınmalı.

- [ ] X postları (taslaklar Claude'da) — #neatHack

- [ ] Teslim: 12 Ekim Pazartesi 06:30–11:25 PDT, resmi neatlogs postunu quote ederek
- [ ] Teslimden sonra EC2 sunucusunu kapat (Claude yapabilir)
EOF

  ROOT: backend/controllers/comments.js:70-79: deleteComment reads `slug` from req.params but never uses it. It looks the comment up with findByPk(commentId) and checks only the owner before calling destroy().
S-171 broken Delete a nonexistent comment id | I signed in as a new user and created an article. DELETE on comment id 999999 returned 404 "Comment not found". DELETE on id 'abc' returned 500 with the raw Postgres error 'invalid input syntax for type integer: "abc"'. I called the API directly and took no screenshots.
  ROOT: backend/controllers/comments.js:72 passes the unvalidated commentId to Comment.findByPk. Postgres throws on the integer cast and the error handler turns it into a 500.

- Ran the 180 P2 and P3 scenarios too. **All 294 scenarios now have a verdict: ✅ 180 · ❌ 104 · ⏭ 10, tracing back to 34 files.** Report: [docs/evidence/findings-conduit-all.md](docs/evidence/findings-conduit-all.md).

  status: 'passed' | 'broken' | 'skipped'
  observed: string
  finding?: Finding
}

const SYSTEM = `You are Crashtest's scenario runner. You run ONE user scenario against a running copy of an app,
the way a real user would, and decide honestly whether it held.

Tools: the Playwright browser tools drive a real browser; the app tools (http_get, read_log, shell) let you call
the API, read server logs, and seed test data. The source code is in your working directory (Read, Grep, Glob).

Rules:
- Set up the starting state the scenario names (create test users and data through the UI or API). Never use real
  people's data.
- Sign in the way a real user does — through the app's sign-in form. Do not hand-write tokens into localStorage or
  cookies; that skips the app's own state setup and produces blank or broken pages that are not real bugs.
- If a page renders blank or half-drawn, read the browser console and network errors before deciding anything.
  A verdict must rest on what you actually checked; if part of the scenario could not be checked, say which part.
- Do the steps in the real app. Take a screenshot at the decisive moment and LOOK at it. Read the browser console
  and server logs. A 200 response is not proof; what the user sees is.
- "passed" means you saw it work. If the app behaves differently from the expected result, it is "broken".
  If a step needs something you do not have (a real third-party reply, a paid plan, a device), it is "skipped" —
  say exactly why. Never call a skipped scenario passed.
- If broken: find the cause in the source code (cite file:line) — the graph tools find handlers, callers and
  blast radius fastest — and write a minimal suggested fix as a unified diff.
  Do not edit any files.
- Keep each run short and focused on this one scenario.`

  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    status: { type: 'string', enum: ['passed', 'broken', 'skipped'] },

        rootCause: { type: 'string', description: 'Why, citing file:line' },
        suggestedFix: { type: 'string', description: 'Unified diff' },
        screenshot: { type: 'string', description: 'Path of the screenshot that shows it' }
      },
      required: ['summary', 'expected', 'actual', 'rootCause', 'suggestedFix']
    }
  },
  required: ['status', 'observed']
}

import { app } from 'electron'
import { join } from 'path'
import type { Finding, Inventory, Scenario } from '../../shared/types'
import type { Runtime } from '../runtime/types'
import { runAgent } from './runAgent'
import { APP_TOOLS, appToolsServer } from './runtimeTools'
import { GRAPH_TOOLS, graphServer } from './graphTools'

export interface SweepVerdict {
  status: 'passed' | 'broken' | 'skipped'
  observed: string
  finding?: Finding
}

const SYSTEM = `You are Crashtest's scenario runner. You run ONE user scenario against a running copy of an app,
the way a real user would, and decide honestly whether it held.

Tools: the Playwright browser tools drive a real browser; the app tools (http_get, read_log, shell) let you call
the API, read server logs, and seed test data. The source code is in your working directory (Read, Grep, Glob).

Rules:
- Set up the starting state the scenario names (create test users and data through the UI or API). Never use real
  people's data.
- Sign in the way a real user does — through the app's sign-in form. Do not hand-write tokens into localStorage or
  cookies; that skips the app's own state setup and produces blank or broken pages that are not real bugs.
- If a page renders blank or half-drawn, read the browser console and network errors before deciding anything.
  A verdict must rest on what you actually checked; if part of the scenario could not be checked, say which part.
- Do the steps in the real app. Take a screenshot at the decisive moment and LOOK at it. Read the browser console
  and server logs. A 200 response is not proof; what the user sees is.
- "passed" means you saw it work. If the app behaves differently from the expected result, it is "broken".
  If a step needs something you do not have (a real third-party reply, a paid plan, a device), it is "skipped" —
  say exactly why. Never call a skipped scenario passed.
- If broken: find the cause in the source code (cite file:line) — the graph tools find handlers, callers and
  blast radius fastest — and write a minimal suggested fix as a unified diff.
  Do not edit any files.
- Keep each run short and focused on this one scenario.`

const SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    status: { type: 'string', enum: ['passed', 'broken', 'skipped'] },
    observed: { type: 'string', description: 'What actually happened, in two or three sentences' },
    finding: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        summary: { type: 'string', description: 'One line bug title' },
        expected: { type: 'string' },
        actual: { type: 'string' },
        rootCause: { type: 'string', description: 'Why, citing file:line' },
        suggestedFix: { type: 'string', description: 'Unified diff' },
        screenshot: { type: 'string', description: 'Path of the screenshot that shows it' }
      },
      required: ['summary', 'expected', 'actual', 'rootCause', 'suggestedFix']
    }
  },
  required: ['status', 'observed']
}

function playwrightServer(outputDir: string): Record<string, unknown> {
  const cli = join(app.getAppPath(), 'node_modules', '@playwright', 'mcp', 'cli.js')
  return {
    playwright: {
      type: 'stdio',
      command: 'node',
      args: [
        cli,
        '--headless',
        '--isolated',
        '--viewport-size',
        '1280,800',
        '--output-dir',
        outputDir
      ]
    }
  }
}

export async function runScenario(opts: {
  projectId: string
  scenario: Scenario
  runtime: Runtime
  localWorkdir: string
  baseUrl: string
  apiUrl: string
  inventory?: Inventory
  signal?: AbortSignal
}): Promise<SweepVerdict> {
  const s = opts.scenario
  const outputDir = join(opts.localWorkdir, '.crashtest', 'shots', s.id)
  const graph = await graphServer(opts.localWorkdir)
  const res = await runAgent<SweepVerdict>({
    projectId: opts.projectId,
    cwd: opts.localWorkdir,
    systemPrompt: SYSTEM,
    prompt:
      `App: ${opts.inventory?.productName ?? ''} — ${opts.inventory?.summary ?? ''}\n` +
      `Open the app at ${opts.baseUrl}${opts.apiUrl && opts.apiUrl !== opts.baseUrl ? ` (API at ${opts.apiUrl})` : ''}.\n\n` +
      `Scenario ${s.id} [${s.priority}] — ${s.title}\nWho: ${s.who}\nStarting state: ${s.startingState}\n` +
      `Steps:\n${s.steps.map((x, i) => `${i + 1}. ${x}`).join('\n')}\nExpected: ${s.expected}\n\n` +
      `Save screenshots into ${outputDir}. Run it now and report the verdict.`,
    allowedTools: [
      'Read',
      'Grep',
      'Glob',
      'mcp__playwright',
      ...APP_TOOLS,
      ...(Object.keys(graph).length ? GRAPH_TOOLS : [])
    ],
    mcpServers: {
      ...playwrightServer(outputDir),
      ...(await appToolsServer(opts.runtime)),
      ...graph
    },
    schema: SCHEMA,
    maxTurns: 40,
    signal: opts.signal
  })
  return res.output
}
